mechanism: Both drugs cause CNS depression and mefloquine can inhibit CYP3A4, potentially increasing zolpidem levels and enhancing sedative effects; mefloquine also carries independent neuropsychiatric risks including seizures and hallucinations.
action: Avoid combination if possible; if necessary, reduce zolpidem dose significantly, monitor closely for excessive sedation, confusion, and neuropsychiatric symptoms, and consider alternative antimalarial agents.
